chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleym, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man permits his slave girl to his brother.' He said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'Supposing she were to come with a child?' He said, 'He would keep his child and return the slave girl to her owner.' I said, 'Supposing he had not permitted to him regarding that?' He said, 'He had permitted for him, and it was not safe for that to happen.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave girl bearing a child after being permitted to another man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the fiqh of 'tamlik al-jariya' (granting concubinage rights) within the context of early Shia jurisprudence, specifically addressing the lineage attribution (walad) when a slave girl is shared. It establishes that the child belongs to the brother who consummated the union, while the woman reverts to her original owner, highlighting the principle that implied permission suffices for procreation unless explicitly restricted. This ruling reflects the scholarly consensus on the distinction between ownership rights and reproductive rights in pre-modern Islamic family law.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleym, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man permits his slave girl to his brother. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. So I said, ‘(supposing) she were to come with a child?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His child would be entrusted to him and the slave girl returned to her owner’. I said, ‘Supposing he had not permitted to him regarding that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He had permitted for him, and it was not safe for that to happen’.
